messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Pager: Elevated TLS handshake failures + 5xx to /v1/generate from EU edge POPs. Alert group: api-cdn-eu. See alert: https://grafana.redwood/api/alerts/8232

aisha (oncall): Ack. I'm seeing a big spike from eu-west and eu-central. 525s and 524s mostly. Customer traffic impacted for EU -> high latency and occasional connection resets.

priya (sre): digging in — quick dig from my laptop: 
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai
93.184.216.34
(then intermittently:) ;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
Some resolvers return address, some time out. TTLs look normal.

jonas (infra): my side: origin logs show TLS errors when Cloudflare connects: "SSL_connect returned=1 errno=0 state=SSLv3 read server hello A: sslv3 alert handshake failure". This started ~10:02 UTC. Cloudflare monitors also pinging with intermittent SERVFAILs.

cf-monitor-bot: Cloudflare: Investigating: Edge TLS handshakes failing in EU region (EUROPE). Ticket created: https://support.cloudflare.com/ticket/REDACTED

aisha (oncall): Action plan: (1) temporarily fail traffic to EU POPs -> route to global fallback pool (us-east + us-west) via routing policy (2) enable secondary DNS provider failover if routing doesn't fix reachability (3) communicate to customers. I'll make the routing change now.

jonas (infra): I'm running the LB policy switch: 
```
# switching traffic steering policy to prefer fallback pool
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $LB_API" "https://api.loadbalancer.redwood/v1/route/policy/steer" -d '{"policy":"prefer-fallback-eu","ttl":30}'
```
Applying... 

jonas (infra): ok policy toggled. TTL 30s. Should see client connections drift to fallback pool in ~30s.

priya (sre): running quick checks: 
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:93.184.216.34
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (93.184.216.34) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to api.redwood.ai:443
```
Still seeing handshake errors from some paths. Fallback is in progress though; metrics show EU requests to fallback pool increasing.

eva (support): drafting status update. Proposed copy: "We are currently investigating intermittent connectivity issues affecting API access from some EU regions. We're rerouting traffic and working with our CDN provider. No data loss. We'll update within 30 minutes." Approve? :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

aisha (oncall): Approve. Post to status and cc enterprise customers via email template 3.

incident-bot: Status page draft posted to staging: https://status.redwood/ops/incident/2409876543-draft

priya (sre): Additional observation: dig +trace shows delegations returning inconsistent NS sets from our primary DNS provider intermittently. Sample: 
```
;; Received 2 responses, 1 truncated
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 1234
```
Could be a resolver propagation issue coupled with CF edge state.

jonas (infra): I can trigger DNS failover to secondary provider (preconfigured) if we still see > 10% errors after 10m. Ready to flip via API: `POST /dns/failover?to=secondary&force=true`.

aisha (oncall): Let’s give routing 10 mins. If errors persist, flip DNS. Priya, keep running traces and collect sample dig/curl outputs for postmortem.

(9 minutes pass)

priya (sre): 10m in — errors dropped from 46% -> 12% overall. Most customer traffic now in fallback pool but latency higher for EU customers. Cloudflare support says they see abnormal handshake errors for some EU POPs; they’re triaging.

jonas (infra): holding DNS failover for now. Flipping would increase TTL churn and might disrupt current connections. Recommend keeping traffic steer.

mason (oncall-2): I'm picking up the on-call handoff from Aisha in 20 mins. Anything I should watch?

aisha (oncall): Passing baton to @mason. Steps completed: routing policy toggled -> EU -> fallback pool, status update posted, Cloudflare ticket open. Remaining: monitor handshake error rate and decide on DNS flip if >15% errors persist for 15m. Docs: runbook -> /runbooks/cloudflare-dns-failover.md.

mason (oncall-2): Ack. I'll monitor dashboards and coordinate with support to send another customer update if impact continues.

eva (support): Customer message ready for enterprise: "We are experiencing degraded connectivity for EU-based requests. We have rerouted traffic to maintain availability and are actively working with our CDN provider to restore normal routing. We will follow up with technical details and ETA." Sending to affected accounts now.

(30 minutes pass)

priya (sre): Cloudflare reported mitigation on their side for the affected POP cluster — they pushed a config restart. Handshake errors are gradually returning to baseline. Current error rate ~2.1% EU, latency trending down.

jonas (infra): Rolling back steering policy to normal gradually (increase weight back to eu pools). Doing staged rollback now.

jonas (infra): rollback complete. Traffic back to normal weighting. Monitoring for 15m.

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded from SEV2 -> SEV3 (reduced customer impact, mitigation in place).

aisha (oncall): Great work team. Quick retrospectives items for postmortem: (1) improve automated detection for DNS delegation anomalies, (2) re-run DNS failover playbook to ensure flip is seamless, (3) confirm Cloudflare escalation contacts + runbook timing. Priya, Jonas — can you own the data collection for the postmortem?

priya (sre): Will collect dig/curl traces, LB routing adjustments, and Cloudflare ticket logs.

jonas (infra): I'll capture LB API calls and the exact timestamps for routing change + rollback.

mason (oncall-2): Taking over for the next shift. If anything pops, ping @mason and I’ll wake up.

eva (support): Final customer update queued: "Issue largely mitigated; degraded performance resolved. If you see residual issues, please open a support ticket." Sending now. :email: 

incident-bot: Handoff note created and assigned to mason (oncall-2). Closing the active pager.

(Next steps logged)

aisha (oncall): End of incident comments: root cause suspected: transient DNS delegation/resolver inconsistency causing Cloudflare edge to route traffic to misconfigured/old POPs resulting in TLS handshake failures. Cloudflare investigating root cause on their edge. Postmortem owners: priya, jonas. ETA for draft: 48 hours.

mason (oncall-2): Ack. I'll add a short timeline + customer impact table to the postmortem once priya/jonas upload artifacts.

incident-bot: Incident thread archived.
